claim: In 2023-24 studies, some chatbots (mainly GPT-4, also ChatGPT-3 and Copy.ai in Koivisto and Grassini) scored higher than the average human on semantic-distance originality in the AUT (fluency controlled or matched) and in the DAT (GPT-4 over humans; other models such as Gemini Pro were indistinguishable from humans, and Haase and Hanel found no mean AUT difference); in one-shot tasks the best humans still matched or beat the best AI (Koivisto and Grassini; top human decile/quartile beat every DAT model in Bellemare-Pepin).
agent_test: Score our agent vs plain model on AUT/DAT items at equal tokens with SemDis and human or LLM raters; report mean and max, and fluency-controlled.
audit_note: Haase and Hanel (listed as support) found no mean originality difference between chatbots and humans, and in Bellemare-Pepin only some LLMs (GPT-4, 'several leading LLMs') beat the human DAT mean while Gemini Pro did not; fluency was matched only in the Hubert AUT; evidence is from 2023-24 chatbots and mostly GPT-4.
claim_before_audit: At matched fluency, frontier LLMs score higher than the average human on semantic-distance originality in the AUT and DAT; in one-shot tasks the best humans still match or beat them.

claim: The LLM advantage is not stable across model versions and conditions: GPT-4o (Feb 2025) scored well below GPT-4 (2023) on DAT, and model means vary widely on DAT but are tight on AUT.
agent_test: Fix prompt, model snapshot and rater; rerun the same DAT set across several snapshots to measure drift before comparing arms.
note: d08: across 54 models DT diversity benchmarks fall -0.47 z/year while creative writing rises; supports drift but measures diversity, not DAT originality.

claim: LLM ideas are homogeneous across samples and across models: within-model pairwise similarity is above 0.8 for most open-ended queries; population variability is far below humans even when individual originality is equal. Caveat (d05): the 0.8 threshold is judged against an undemanding null; for same-prompt but genuinely different ideas the median cosine is already about 0.70-0.72 and 20-32% of pairs exceed 0.8, though a residual 2-3x effect remains.
agent_test: Measure pairwise embedding similarity and NoveltyBench distinct-k for 10 samples per prompt for plain vs scaffold at equal tokens.

claim: Raising temperature does not reliably produce more divergent output: small novelty gain with more incoherence, no link to AUT flexibility, and min-p still leaves 61% of pairs above 0.8 similarity.
schema_part: G (do not rely on sampling for diversity)
agent_test: Compare temperature sweep vs structured diversification at equal tokens on distinct-k and rated quality.
audit_note: Stevenson's no-temperature link covers only GPT-3 at temperature 0.65-0.80, and Bellemare-Pepin (also listed) found GPT-4 DAT scores rise with temperature, so 'not reliably' is a hedged but narrow reading; 61.2% above 0.8 is at min-p default sampling (Jiang et al).

claim: Originality and utility were negatively correlated within responses (r = -.56 for humans, r = -.61 for GPT-3, Stevenson et al 2022); higher temperature gave slightly more novel but more incoherent stories (Peeperkorn et al 2024), so open-mode metrics should score both novelty and usefulness or coherence.
agent_test: Report originality and utility together; accept an idea set only if utility is above a floor.
audit_note: r = -.56 (humans) and -.61 (GPT-3) is confirmed in Stevenson, but neither source shows originality rising with temperature or prompts while usefulness falls; Peeperkorn measures novelty vs coherence/typicality, not usefulness.
claim_before_audit: Originality and utility trade off (r about -.56 to -.61); semantic-distance originality can be raised by temperature or prompts while usefulness falls, so open-mode metrics need both axes.

claim: Prompt strategy and task-awareness change LLM divergent scores: naming the DAT raised percentile by 11.9 points on average, etymology prompts helped, opposition prompts hurt, a 'be creative' system prompt gives small gains.
agent_test: A/B scaffold diverge prompts vs plain at equal tokens on DAT and AUT.
audit_note: 'Naming the DAT' is the paper's aware vs unaware condition (B = 11.89 percentile points over 14 LLMs, Haase and Hanel 2025).

claim: Verbalized sampling and multi-sample regeneration restore diversity (x1.6-2.1 on creative writing; regeneration matches human-writer diversity on NoveltyBench).
agent_test: Implement list-then-dedupe divergence and compare distinct-k and quality at equal total tokens vs best-of-N.
audit_note: VS gain is 1.6-2.1x diversity over direct prompting in creative writing (Zhang et al); 'restore' is loose since VS recovers about two thirds of base-model diversity; NoveltyBench in-context regeneration roughly matches human-writer diversity for three models.

claim: LLM-generated research ideas were rated more novel than expert ideas (5.64 vs 4.84) but the pool saturates: only about 200 of 4000 seeds were non-duplicate.
schema_part: O (diverge + dedupe); memory of seen ideas
agent_test: Track duplicate rate with a seen-idea memory and stop generating when new non-duplicate share drops under a threshold.

claim: DT is only modestly related to intelligence (r about .25) and depends on instruction and scoring; there is no threshold effect (replication).
schema_part: none (justifies not using Gf-style tests as creativity proxy)
agent_test: Check correlation of our agent's AUT scores with its reasoning benchmark scores across arms.

claim: DT test performance predicts other creative outcomes weakly, supporting Runco's point that DT is not all of creativity.
schema_part: S-open (do not use DT alone as the open-mode metric)
agent_test: Add a second open-mode metric (e.g. real task with problem solution novelty) and see if arm ranking agrees with AUT.

claim: Automated semantic-distance and LLM scoring track human ratings (r .45-.91 depending on study, ICC>=.80 for LLM scorers) but are confounded by fluency and elaboration and do not generalise to all creativity measures.
agent_test: Use two scorers (embedding distance and LLM rater) and require agreement; control for response length.
audit_note: Lower bound r=.45 not located in opened sources (found .55 Koivisto, .78-.94 Haase and Hanel, latent .91 SemDis); ICC>=.80 for LLM scorers comes via a 2026 review citing Organisciak, not a primary check.

claim: LLM-assisted human ideation homogenises group output (fewer distinct ideas), although it widens category coverage.
agent_test: Compare idea-set diversity for user-alone vs user-plus-agent sessions.
note: d10: strategy lists lowered later solo originality (p=.009) and similarity rose (p=.017) but idea lists did not differ from no-LLM.

claim: LLM creative process measures (switching/jumps) are less reliable than human ones (test-retest .22 vs .42) and temperature does not change AUT jumps.
agent_test: Do not rely on single-run process metrics; average over at least 10 runs.

claim: Model-internal steering of vocabulary matches prompting on DAT but shifts which words appear; baselines concentrate 25.5% of tokens on top-10 words and share repeated words across model families.
agent_test: Add a ban list of the model's own frequent words (microscope, elephant, ocean) and measure DAT and overlap.

claim: Serial-order effect (later ideas more original) is robust but tiny (variance explained at most 3.5%), so 'keep generating' helps little per extra idea.
agent_test: Plot originality vs generation index for agent output and set the stop point.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-03 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: A scaffold that separates goal-blind divergent generation from a later narrowing step raised judged originality and path discovery for GPT-5.4 (AUT originality 2.91 to 3.77; MUTATE paths 27/56 to 38/56), but no equal-token control exists.
schema_part: O-diverge then O-converge (separate calls, goal withheld in diverge)
agent_test: Run diverge-then-select against best-of-2 and verbalized sampling at equal tokens on AUT and DAT.

claim: Short explicit divergence instructions ('wild, bold, unconventional') raise novelty about as well as or better than long method prompts (SCAMPER, TRIZ, C-K); homogenization across models persists.
agent_test: Compare a one-line divergence cue with a SCAMPER-style multistep prompt on equal tokens.
audit_note: Rests mainly on IDEAFix (simple 'wild/unconventional' prompts outperform method prompts, homogenization persists across models); Schaeffer partly supports and CreativityNeuro is weight steering, not prompting.

claim: Verbalized-distribution prompting beats direct, CoT, sequence and multi-turn at the same N-response budget on creative-writing diversity (x1.6-2.1); typicality bias in preference data (beta 0.57-0.65) is the proposed cause.
schema_part: O-diverge (ask for several with probabilities, pick low-probability ones)
agent_test: Replicate on AUT/DAT with fluency matched.

claim: Semantic-distance tests predict LLM creative writing and diversity benchmarks (DAT validity .51-.71, CDAT .63 on NoveltyBench) but none of the existing tests predicts scientific ideation; capability confounds scores (r up to .98).
schema_part: S-open metrics (use a task-grounded second metric)
agent_test: Check our agent on a science-ideation set as well as DAT.

claim: Consensus-avoidance methods (persona anchoring, anti-modal prompts, sample-then-ban common phrases) raise embedding diversity more than temperature or min-p does; min-p has no demonstrated diversity benefit in its own human data.
schema_part: O-diverge (sample K, find modal answer, forbid it)
agent_test: Measure distinct-idea count, not only embedding spread.

claim: Random remote analogy sources help humans at almost any distance but help LLMs only when the source is far and the model is strong.
agent_test: Test remote-seed insertion by model strength.
